input_case:
History of Present Illness:
68-year-old woman. Severe epigastric pain began six hours after an endoscopic biliary procedure yesterday. She has vomited repeatedly.

Physical Examination:
Epigastric tenderness and reduced bowel sounds; no generalized rigidity. Temperature 38.3 C; heart rate 106/min; BP 134/70 mmHg; respiratory rate 18/min; SpO2 98% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 15.1 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.1 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 241 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 136 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.7 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 72 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 1130 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 31 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 28 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 91 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
CT abdomen: diffuse pancreatic edema and peripancreatic fat stranding. No free air or organized collection.
